ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AB=BC$, $AD \perp BC$ at point $D$, $CE$ bisects $\angle ACB$, intersects $AB$ at point $E$, and intersects $AD$ at point $P$. If $\angle B=x^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle APE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $AB=BC$ and $\angle B=x^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle BAC=\angle ACB$,\\
thus $\angle ACB= \frac{1}{2}(180^\circ-\angle B)= \frac{1}{2}(180^\circ-x^\circ)=90^\circ- \frac{1}{2}x^\circ$;\\
Since $CE$ bisects $\angle ACB$,\\
then $\angle DCP= \frac{1}{2}\angle ACB= \frac{1}{2}(90^\circ- \frac{1}{2}x^\circ)=45^\circ- \frac{1}{4}x^\circ$;\\
Since $AD \perp BC$,\\
then $\angle ADC=90^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle APE=\angle DPC=90^\circ-\angle DCP=90^\circ-(45^\circ- \frac{1}{4}x^\circ)=45^\circ+ \frac{1}{4}x^\circ.$\\
Therefore, the answer is: $\boxed{45^\circ+\frac{1}{4}x^\circ}$.

It can be seen in the figure that A, P, D are on the same straight line, and E, P, C are on the same straight line. In right triangle DPC, ∠DPC=90°-∠DCP=90°-(45°-x°/4)=45°+x°/4. It can be seen from the figure that PA and PD are opposite rays on AD, and PE and PC are opposite rays on CE, therefore ∠APE and ∠DPC are vertical angles and are equal. Therefore ∠APE=45°+x°/4.
